questions.q: A disk of 128 MB uses 2 KB blocks and a FAT with 2-byte entries (one entry per block). What is the size of the FAT?
questions.exp: Blocks = 128 MB / 2 KB = 65,536 entries; × 2 B = 131,072 B = 128 KB.

questions.q: In a microkernel design:
options: all OS services including file systems and drivers run in kernel space
there is no kernel at all
applications run in kernel mode for speed
only minimal services (IPC, basic scheduling, memory management) run in kernel space and other services run in user space
questions.exp: A microkernel keeps the kernel small; the cost is extra message-passing overhead between user-space servers.

questions.q: In two-level paging with a 32-bit address, 12-bit offset and a 10-bit outer-page index, how many bits index the inner page table?
In a system with 32-bit logical addresses, 4 KB pages and 4-byte page-table entries, what is the size of a single-level page table?
questions.exp: Entries = 2^20; size = 2^20 × 4 B = 4 MB.

questions.q: Non-preemptive SJF: P1 (arrival 0, burst 7), P2 (2, 4), P3 (4, 1), P4 (5, 4). What is the average waiting time?
Memory access time is 200 ns and servicing a page fault takes 8 ms. If the page-fault rate is 1 in 1000 accesses, what is the effective access time (approximately)?

questions.exp: Two successive forks create 2² = 4 processes, and each prints A once.

questions.q: The 'ostrich algorithm' for deadlocks means:
options: ignoring the problem and assuming it rarely occurs
using the Banker's algorithm at each request
questions.exp: Systems like UNIX and Windows largely ignore deadlock because prevention and detection are costly.

questions.q: The disk head is at cylinder 50. The request queue (in arrival order) is 82, 170, 43, 140, 24, 16, 190. What is the total head movement under FCFS?
An inverted page table has:
options: one entry for each logical page of every process
one entry for each physical frame
one entry for each disk block
one entry for each TLB line only
questions.exp: It is indexed by frame and stores (process id, page number), reducing table size at the cost of search time.

questions.q: Head at cylinder 50; request queue 82, 170, 43, 140, 24, 16, 190. What is the total head movement under SSTF?
Reference string: 1,2,3,2,1,4,5,2,1,2,3,4 with 4 frames and LRU. How many page faults occur?
In the first readers-writers problem (readers have priority), the main risk is:
questions.exp: If readers keep arriving, a writer may wait indefinitely because new readers are allowed in while others are reading. The second variant favours writers and can starve readers.

questions.q: The primary role of an operating system is to:
options: translate high-level programs into machine code
act as a resource manager and provide an interface between user and hardware
create hardware drivers only for printers
store data permanently on the disk
questions.exp: The OS allocates CPU, memory and I/O devices and offers services to users and applications.

questions.q: A device driver is best described as:
options: an application used to install programs
kernel-level software that lets the OS communicate with a hardware device controller
a hardware component inside the disk
a type of CPU scheduling policy
questions.exp: Device drivers provide a uniform interface between the OS and the device-specific hardware.

questions.q: A system has 6 identical resources and each process needs exactly 2 of them. What is the maximum number of processes that can be in the system with deadlock never occurring?
questions.exp: Deadlock-free requires n(2-1) + 1 ≤ 6, i.e. n ≤ 5.

questions.q: The disk head is at cylinder 100. Requests arrive in the order 30, 160, 120, 60, 180. What is the total head movement under FCFS?
Which of the following is NOT an operating system?
questions.exp: Firefox is a web browser application; the others are operating systems.

questions.q: The principle of least privilege states that:
options: all users should have administrator rights
a user or program should be given only the access rights needed to do its task
access rights should never be revoked
only the kernel may run programs
questions.exp: Least privilege limits damage from errors or attacks by restricting each domain to the minimum rights necessary.

questions.q: A Unix-like inode has 10 direct pointers and 1 single-indirect pointer. Block size is 1 KB and a block pointer is 4 bytes. What is the maximum file size?
questions.exp: A single-indirect block holds 1024/4 = 256 pointers; total blocks = 10 + 256 = 266, so 266 KB.

questions.q: For using a semaphore to enforce mutual exclusion among processes, the semaphore is initialised to:
questions.exp: A binary semaphore initialised to 1 lets exactly one process enter the critical section.

questions.q: The test-and-set instruction is useful for implementing locks because it:
options: works only on a single-processor system
reads and sets a memory word as one atomic operation
questions.exp: Atomicity ensures only one process can acquire the lock; the resulting spinlock still uses busy waiting.

questions.q: TLB hit ratio is 80%, TLB lookup takes 20 ns and a memory access takes 100 ns (single-level page table). What is the effective access time?
Which directory structure allows a file to be shared among users without making copies, but needs care to avoid dangling references?
options: Simple tree directory with no links
questions.exp: Acyclic-graph directories permit shared files or subdirectories through links.

questions.q: The Linux kernel is classified as:
options: a monolithic kernel with loadable modules
questions.exp: Linux runs most services in kernel space but supports dynamically loadable modules.

questions.q: Non-preemptive priority scheduling (smaller number = higher priority): P1 (arrival 0, burst 4, priority 3), P2 (1, 3, priority 1), P3 (2, 2, priority 2). What is the waiting time of P3?
questions.exp: P1 runs 0-4, then P2 4-7, then P3 7-9. P3 waits 7 - 2 = 5 ms.

questions.q: Linux allows device drivers and file systems to be added to a running kernel without rebooting through:
questions.exp: Linux is a monolithic kernel that supports dynamically loadable kernel modules (insmod/modprobe), giving modular flexibility without microkernel message-passing overhead.

questions.q: The Optimal page replacement algorithm is not practical because it:
options: needs knowledge of future page references
questions.exp: It replaces the page that will not be used for the longest time, which cannot be known in advance; it serves as a benchmark.

questions.q: Reference string: 2,3,2,1,5,2,4,5,3,2,5,2 with 3 frames and LRU. How many page faults occur?
questions.exp: Faults at 2,3,1,5,4,3,2 = 7; the remaining five references are hits.

questions.q: Direct Memory Access (DMA) is used to:
options: transfer blocks of data between a device and memory without CPU involvement for each byte
increase the clock speed of the CPU
questions.exp: The DMA controller moves data directly and interrupts the CPU only after the whole transfer finishes.

questions.q: Which statement distinguishes livelock from deadlock?
options: Livelock requires a minimum of four processes
In livelock, processes keep changing state but make no progress
Livelock occurs only in single-processor systems
In livelock, processes are blocked forever without any activity
questions.exp: Livelocked processes are not blocked; they actively respond to each other yet never finish.

questions.q: External fragmentation in contiguous memory allocation can be reduced by:
questions.exp: Compaction shuffles processes to merge scattered free holes into one large block.

questions.q: A disk has average seek time 6 ms, rotates at 6000 RPM and has 100 sectors per track. What is the average time to read one sector?
questions.exp: Rotation = 10 ms; average latency 5 ms; transfer = 10/100 = 0.1 ms; total = 6 + 5 + 0.1 = 11.1 ms.

questions.q: Which statement about shell redirection is correct?
options: > overwrites the target file whereas >> appends to it
Both read input from the file
questions.exp: cmd > f truncates f first; cmd >> f appends output at the end.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT stored in the Process Control Block (PCB) of a process?
options: The complete source code of the program
The process state and process ID
questions.exp: The PCB holds execution context and bookkeeping information (PC, registers, state, PID, scheduling data), not the source code.

questions.q: In the output of ls -l, a line beginning with the character 'd' (for example drwxr-xr-x) represents:
questions.exp: The first character shows the file type: d for directory, - for regular file, l for symbolic link.

questions.q: The kernels of Windows NT and macOS are best described as:
options: hybrid kernels (microkernel ideas with monolithic components)
questions.exp: Hybrid kernels combine a microkernel-style design with some services kept in kernel space for speed. Windows NT and macOS (XNU) are standard examples; Linux is monolithic with loadable modules.

questions.q: Under FCFS, processes arrive at time 0 in the order P1 (burst 24), P2 (burst 3), P3 (burst 3). What is the average waiting time?
questions.exp: Waiting times are 0, 24 and 27, so the average is 51/3 = 17 ms.

questions.q:
Statement I: Paging eliminates external fragmentation.
Statement II: Pure segmentation suffers mainly from internal fragmentation.
Which option is correct?
questions.exp: Paging uses fixed-size frames so there is no external fragmentation; segmentation uses variable sizes and suffers external fragmentation.

questions.q: Deadlock can be prevented by breaking circular wait through:
options: allowing processes to hold resources while waiting
imposing a total ordering on resource types and requesting resources in that order
questions.exp: If every process requests resources in increasing order of number, a cycle cannot form.

questions.q: In the five-state process model, a running process moves to the ready state when:
options: the I/O it was waiting for completes
it is first created by the system
questions.exp: Timer interrupt at the end of the quantum preempts the running process and places it in the ready queue; I/O request leads to blocked state.

questions.q: Which interprocess communication mechanism is generally the fastest once it has been set up?
questions.exp: After setup, shared memory accesses need no system calls or kernel copying, unlike message passing.

questions.q: In a batch operating system:
options: similar jobs are collected and executed together with no user interaction during execution
users interact with every job through terminals in real time
the CPU is shared in equal time slices among users
questions.exp: Batch systems group jobs with similar needs and run them sequentially without interaction.

questions.q: The medium-term scheduler is mainly responsible for:
options: selecting the next ready process to run on the CPU
swapping processes out of and back into main memory
admitting new jobs from the job pool into memory
questions.exp: Medium-term scheduling reduces the degree of multiprogramming by swapping out processes and later swapping them in.

questions.q: Which free-space management method keeps one bit for every disk block?
questions.exp: A bit vector stores one bit per block (free or allocated). Linked list, grouping and counting store block addresses or (address, count) pairs instead.

questions.q: During system start-up, the bootstrap loader (boot loader) is responsible for:
options: locating and loading the operating system kernel into main memory
questions.exp: After firmware (BIOS/UEFI) tests the hardware, the boot loader loads the kernel and passes control to it.

questions.q: A buffer in I/O management is:
options: a memory area that temporarily holds data while it is transferred between two entities
a hardware port for the keyboard
questions.exp: Buffers cope with speed mismatch between producer and consumer of data.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Time-sharing systems provide good interactive response.
Reason (R): The CPU is switched among users after a small time quantum.
Which option is correct?
options: A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
questions.exp: Rapid switching with a small quantum gives each user quick turns on the CPU, which explains the good response.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT stored in the inode of a Unix file?
questions.exp: The file name is stored in the directory entry, which maps the name to an inode number.

questions.q: A system has 32-bit logical addresses and 4 KB pages. How many bits are used for the page number?
questions.exp: 4 KB = 2^12, so the offset is 12 bits and the page number is 32 - 12 = 20 bits.

questions.q: In demand paging, a page-table entry whose valid-invalid bit is "invalid" means that the page:
options: is not in main memory (or is not part of the process address space)
questions.exp: An invalid bit signals that the page is not currently in physical memory (or the address is illegal). Access causes a trap; if the page is legal, the OS brings it in (page fault).

questions.q: A malicious program that replicates itself and spreads across a network without needing a host file or user action is called a:
questions.exp: A worm is self-replicating and propagates on its own through the network. A virus needs a host file/user action, a Trojan hides inside a useful program, and a logic bomb triggers on a condition.

questions.q: A process of size 72,766 bytes is loaded in a paging system with 2048-byte pages. How much internal fragmentation occurs in its last page?
questions.exp: 72,766 = 35 × 2048 + 1086, so 36 pages are needed; waste = 2048 - 1086 = 962 bytes.

questions.q: Which scheduling algorithm gives the minimum average waiting time for a given set of processes that are all available at the same time?
questions.exp: SJF is provably optimal for minimizing average waiting time.

questions.q: The Banker's algorithm is an example of:
questions.exp: Banker's algorithm checks that each allocation leaves the system in a safe state before granting it.

questions.q: Seek time of a disk is the time required to:
options: move the read/write head to the desired cylinder
rotate the desired sector under the head
questions.exp: Seek time is the head-positioning time; rotational latency and transfer time are separate.

questions.q: Match the file systems with their typical operating systems: (i) ext4 (ii) NTFS (iii) APFS. Which mapping is correct?
questions.exp: ext4 is the common Linux file system, NTFS is Windows, APFS is Apple's file system for macOS and iOS.

questions.q: Round Robin with time quantum 3 ms. P1, P2, P3 all arrive at 0 with bursts 7, 4 and 2 ms respectively (in that order). At what time does P2 complete?
Head at cylinder 50 moving toward cylinder 0 on a disk with cylinders 0-199; queue 82, 170, 43, 140, 24, 16, 190. What is the total head movement under SCAN?
questions.exp: 50 → 0 costs 50 (servicing 43, 24, 16), then 0 → 190 costs 190; total 240.

questions.q: Match the system with its category: (i) VxWorks (ii) MS-DOS (iii) UNIX. Which mapping is correct?
options: (i) single-user OS, (ii) multi-user OS, (iii) real-time OS
(i) Real-time OS, (ii) single-user single-tasking OS, (iii) multi-user multitasking OS
(i) real-time OS, (ii) multi-user OS, (iii) single-user OS
(i) multi-user OS, (ii) real-time OS, (iii) single-user OS
questions.exp: VxWorks is an RTOS, MS-DOS ran one task at a time for one user, and UNIX supports many users and processes.

questions.q: Contiguous file allocation has which of the following disadvantages?
options: External fragmentation and difficulty in growing a file
A pointer is needed in every block
questions.exp: Contiguous allocation gives fast sequential and direct access but suffers external fragmentation and file growth problems.

questions.q: Which statement about linked allocation of disk blocks is correct?
options: It requires the file size to be known at creation
It needs no space for pointers
It does not support efficient direct access to the middle of a file
questions.exp: To reach block k, the k preceding blocks must be traversed through their pointers.

questions.q: Head at cylinder 50 moving toward higher cylinders; queue 82, 170, 43, 140, 24, 16, 190. What is the total head movement under LOOK?
questions.exp: 50 → 190 costs 140, then 190 → 16 costs 174; total 314.

questions.q: Page size is 1 KB and page 2 of a process is mapped to frame 7. What physical address corresponds to logical address 2100?
How many simultaneous disk failures can a RAID 5 array tolerate without losing data?
questions.exp: RAID 5 uses block striping with distributed single parity, so any one failed disk can be rebuilt from the others. A second failure before rebuild loses data (RAID 6 tolerates two).

questions.q: A time-sharing operating system achieves good response time for many users by:
options: giving each user a dedicated CPU
running one job to completion at a time
switching the CPU rapidly among users' programs using a small time slice
questions.exp: Time slicing makes each user feel they have a dedicated machine.

questions.q: In the Banker's algorithm, if Max for a process is (7, 5, 3) and its current Allocation is (0, 1, 0), what is its Need vector?
questions.exp: Need = Max - Allocation = (7-0, 5-1, 3-0) = (7, 4, 3).

questions.q: Demand paging works efficiently mainly because of:
questions.exp: Programs tend to access a small set of pages repeatedly, so few page faults occur.

questions.q: In the one-to-one multithreading model:
options: all user threads share a single kernel thread
kernel threads are created only for the main thread
user threads cannot run in parallel on multiprocessors
each user thread maps to its own kernel thread, so one blocking call does not block the others
questions.exp: One-to-one (Linux, Windows) gives true parallelism on multiprocessors and avoids blocking the entire process, at the cost of creating a kernel thread per user thread.

questions.q: In a two-level directory structure, file-name collisions between different users are avoided because:
options: each user has a separate User File Directory under a Master File Directory
all file names must be unique across the whole system
only absolute path names are allowed
questions.exp: The Master File Directory (MFD) points to a User File Directory (UFD) per user, so two users can each have a file with the same name. Name collision remains possible only within one user.

questions.q: A counting semaphore is initialised to 2. Five processes each execute a P (wait) operation and none executes V. How many processes are blocked?
questions.exp: The first two P operations succeed (value 0); the remaining three block.

questions.q: A user program requests a kernel service by executing a:
questions.exp: A system call is invoked through a trap, which switches the CPU to kernel mode and runs the handler.

questions.q: The main purpose of journaling in file systems such as ext4 and NTFS is to:
options: keep the file system consistent and speed up recovery after a crash
questions.exp: Changes are logged before being applied, so after a crash the log can be replayed to restore consistency.

questions.q: The Unix utility fsck is used to:
options: check and repair file-system consistency after a crash
questions.exp: fsck compares directory structure, inode link counts and block bitmaps and repairs inconsistencies. Journaling file systems reduce the need for a full fsck.

questions.q: The UNIX operating system was originally developed at:
questions.exp: Ken Thompson and Dennis Ritchie developed UNIX at Bell Labs around 1969-1971.

questions.q: A file /home/a.txt has one hard link /home/b.txt and one symbolic link /home/c.txt to it. If a.txt is deleted, which statement is true?
options: c.txt still works but b.txt does not
b.txt still gives access to the data but c.txt becomes a dangling link
Both b.txt and c.txt become invalid
Both b.txt and c.txt remain valid
questions.exp: The inode survives as long as a hard link remains; the symbolic link only stores the path and breaks.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of the "something you are" authentication factor?
questions.exp: Biometrics (fingerprint, iris, face) are "something you are". Passwords are "something you know"; smart cards and OTP tokens are "something you have".

questions.q: A wait-for graph is used to detect deadlock when:
options: each resource type has only one instance
questions.exp: A wait-for graph is obtained from the resource-allocation graph by removing resource nodes and works for single instances.

questions.q: The exec() family of system calls:
options: waits for the child to finish
replaces the current process image with a new program while keeping the same PID
questions.exp: exec loads a new program into the calling process's address space; no new process is created.

questions.q: A file of size 10 KB is stored on a disk with 4 KB blocks. How much space is lost to internal fragmentation?
questions.exp: 3 blocks (12 KB) are used for 10 KB of data, so 2 KB is wasted in the last block.

questions.q: The convoy effect in FCFS scheduling refers to:
options: processes being starved by higher-priority processes
short processes waiting behind one long CPU-bound process
many processes simultaneously requesting the same device
repeated preemption of processes of equal priority
questions.exp: A long CPU-bound process holding the CPU forces many short I/O-bound processes to wait, lowering utilization.

questions.q: Which command creates a symbolic (soft) link named mylink pointing to the file data.txt?
questions.exp: ln -s TARGET LINKNAME creates a symbolic link; without -s a hard link is made.

questions.q: Which of the following resources is shared by all threads of the same process?
options: The heap memory and global variables
questions.exp: Threads share code, data, heap and open files; each thread has its own stack, program counter and registers.

questions.q: RAID level 1 provides fault tolerance by:
options: mirroring the data on two disks
questions.exp: RAID 1 writes identical copies to two disks (100% capacity overhead). RAID 0 is striping without redundancy; RAID 5 uses distributed parity.

questions.q: The second-chance (clock) page replacement algorithm makes use of:
options: a reference bit for each page
questions.exp: A page with reference bit 1 gets a second chance (bit cleared), otherwise it is replaced.

questions.q: Which of the following scheduling algorithms is inherently non-preemptive?
questions.exp: FCFS lets a process run until it finishes or blocks; the others can preempt a running process.

questions.q: What is the average rotational latency of a disk rotating at 7200 RPM?
questions.exp: One rotation = 60/7200 s = 8.33 ms; the average latency is half of that, 4.17 ms.

questions.q: Starvation of low-priority processes in priority scheduling is commonly solved by:
questions.exp: Aging gradually raises the priority of a process that has waited long, ensuring it eventually runs.
The child has its own copy of x and prints 15 first; the parent waits, then prints its unchanged x = 10.

questions.q: Which statement correctly compares symmetric and asymmetric encryption?
options: Symmetric uses a public/private key pair; asymmetric uses one shared key
Both use the same key, but asymmetric is faster
Symmetric uses one shared secret key and is faster; asymmetric uses a public/private key pair
Asymmetric encryption needs no keys at all
questions.exp: Symmetric ciphers (DES, AES) share one secret key and are fast; asymmetric ciphers (RSA) use a key pair and suit key exchange and digital signatures.

questions.q: In virtualization, the software layer that creates and manages virtual machines and shares the physical hardware among guest operating systems is called the:
questions.exp: A hypervisor (VMM) virtualises the CPU, memory and devices so several guest OSes run in isolated virtual machines. The bootstrap loader starts the OS, drivers control devices and the shell interprets commands.

questions.q: In segmentation with paging (as in MULTICS and Intel x86 designs):
options: each page is divided into segments
each segment is divided into pages
the whole process is kept in one contiguous segment
questions.exp: Paging each segment removes the external-fragmentation problem of pure segmentation while keeping the programmer's logical view and sharing/protection benefits.

questions.q: A backup that copies only the files changed since the last FULL backup is called a(n):
questions.exp: Differential backups copy changes since the last full backup, so restore needs the full backup plus the latest differential. Incremental copies changes since the last backup of any kind.

questions.q: A multiprocessing operating system is one that:
options: uses two or more CPUs that share memory and I/O devices
runs only one process at a time
allows many users on a terminal
questions.exp: Multiprocessing refers to multiple processors working together under one OS.

questions.q: A system has 12 tape drives. Maximum demands / current allocations: P0 10/5, P1 4/2, P2 9/2. Which sequence is safe?
questions.exp: Available = 12 - 9 = 3; needs: P0 5, P1 2, P2 7. P1 runs → avail 5; P0 runs → avail 10; P2 (7 ≤ 10) runs.

questions.q: In the buddy system, a request for 70 KB is made from a 256 KB free block. What is the internal fragmentation in the block allocated to it?
questions.exp: The 256 KB block is split into 128 KB buddies; 128 KB is allocated, wasting 128 - 70 = 58 KB.

questions.q: If the time quantum in Round Robin scheduling is made extremely large, the algorithm behaves like:
questions.exp: If the quantum exceeds every burst, no process is preempted and processes run in arrival order.

questions.q: A disk has 4 surfaces, 1024 tracks per surface, 64 sectors per track and 512 bytes per sector. What is its capacity?
A race condition occurs when:
options: two processes have the same priority
the outcome depends on the order in which concurrent processes access shared data
a process runs faster than another
questions.exp: Unsynchronized access to shared data makes results depend on scheduling interleaving.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a requirement for a solution to the critical-section problem?
questions.exp: The three requirements are mutual exclusion, progress and bounded waiting.

questions.q: A system has a 64 KB logical address space, 1 KB pages and 32 KB of physical memory. How many frames are there in physical memory?
questions.exp: Number of frames = 32 KB / 1 KB = 32.

questions.q: Embedded operating systems are typically characterized by:
options: small memory footprint and a fixed dedicated function
questions.exp: They are designed for devices such as appliances and controllers with limited resources.

questions.q: In a Round Robin system the time quantum is 2 ms and each context switch takes 0.5 ms. What is the CPU efficiency (useful fraction of time)?
In a resource-allocation graph where resource types have multiple instances, the presence of a cycle:
options: is necessary but not sufficient for deadlock
questions.exp: Another instance may let a process in the cycle finish, so a cycle only signals possible deadlock.

questions.q: A distributed operating system differs from a network operating system in that it:
options: only lets users share files through FTP
makes a collection of computers appear to users as a single coherent system
questions.exp: In a distributed OS the location of resources is transparent; in a network OS users are aware of the separate machines.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a hard real-time system?
options: An aircraft flight-control or pacemaker controller
questions.exp: In hard real-time systems missing a deadline is a failure; streaming is soft real-time.

questions.q: A spinlock is most appropriate when:
options: the waiting threads should sleep to save power
there is only one CPU and the holder is not running
the lock is expected to be held for a very short time on a multiprocessor
the lock will be held for several seconds
questions.exp: Spinning wastes CPU, so it pays off only when the wait is shorter than a context switch.

questions.q: Peterson's solution for two processes uses which shared variables?
options: A single binary semaphore and a counter
questions.exp: Peterson's algorithm uses a flag array to indicate interest and a turn variable to break ties.

questions.q: The degree of multiprogramming is controlled by the:
questions.exp: The long-term (job) scheduler decides how many processes are admitted into memory.

questions.q: In the dining philosophers problem with five philosophers and five chopsticks, which approach avoids deadlock?
options: Give each philosopher a time quantum
Let philosophers eat in parallel without any lock
Let every philosopher pick up the left chopstick first and then the right one
Allow at most four philosophers to sit at the table at the same time
questions.exp: If every philosopher grabs the left chopstick, circular wait occurs; limiting to four ensures at least one can get two chopsticks.

questions.q: In dual-mode operation of an operating system, the mode bit value 0 conventionally indicates:
questions.exp: The mode bit distinguishes the two modes: 0 = kernel (privileged) mode and 1 = user mode. Privileged instructions such as I/O and setting the timer execute only in kernel mode.

questions.q: Setting the setuid bit on an executable file causes the program to run with the privileges of:
questions.exp: With setuid, the effective user ID becomes that of the file owner while executing (e.g. passwd runs as root so it can update the password file).

questions.q: A context switch is best described as:
options: switching the monitor between two applications
moving a process from user mode to kernel mode permanently
saving the state of the current process and loading the state of the next process
copying a file from disk to memory
questions.exp: A context switch stores the PCB state of the outgoing process and restores that of the incoming one; it is pure overhead.

questions.q: Which transition is NOT possible in the standard five-state process model?
questions.exp: A ready process is not running, so it cannot issue an I/O request; only a running process can move to waiting.

questions.q: What values does fork() return on success?
options: -1 in the child and 0 in the parent
The child's PID in the parent and 0 in the child
0 in the parent and the child's PID in the child
questions.exp: fork() returns 0 to the child, the new child's PID to the parent, and -1 on failure.

questions.q: In the FAT file system, the information about the next block of a file is found in:
options: the File Allocation Table entry for the current block
the first byte of the block itself
questions.exp: The FAT stores a chain of cluster numbers; each entry points to the next cluster or an end-of-file marker.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a necessary condition for deadlock?
options: Resource preemption (resources can be forcibly taken away)
questions.exp: The four Coffman conditions are mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption and circular wait; allowing preemption breaks deadlock.

questions.q: Priority inversion happens when:
options: a high-priority process waits for a lock held by a low-priority process that is preempted by a medium-priority process
a low-priority process always runs before higher ones
priorities are assigned in decreasing order
questions.exp: The medium-priority process indirectly delays the high-priority one; priority inheritance is the usual fix.

questions.q: Reference string: 1,2,3,4,1,2,5,1,2,3,4,5 with 3 frames and FIFO replacement. How many page faults occur?
questions.exp: Faults on 1,2,3,4,1,2,5,3,4 (the references to 1,2 after 5 and to 5 at the end are hits) = 9.

questions.q: Response time in CPU scheduling is the time:
options: a process spends waiting in the ready queue in total
from submission until the process completes
a process spends executing on the CPU
from submission of a request until the first response is produced
questions.exp: Response time measures how soon the first output is produced, important for interactive systems.

questions.q: C-SCAN is preferred over SCAN because it:
options: provides a more uniform waiting time
questions.exp: C-SCAN services requests in one direction and returns quickly, so cylinders at either end are treated more fairly.

questions.q: Compared with interrupt-driven I/O, polling:
options: is always faster for slow devices
makes the CPU repeatedly check the device status, wasting CPU time
questions.exp: In polling the CPU busy-waits on a status bit; interrupt-driven I/O lets the CPU do other work.

questions.q:
Statement I: Creating a thread is generally faster and uses fewer resources than creating a process.
Statement II: Threads of the same process have separate address spaces.
Which option is correct?
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.exp: Threads share the address space of their process, so they are lightweight; Statement II is false.

questions.q: Four processes arrive at time 0 with CPU bursts 5, 9, 6 and 2 ms. Under non-preemptive SJF, what is the average waiting time?
questions.exp: Order 2, 5, 6, 9 gives waiting times 0, 2, 7, 13; sum 22, average 5.5.

questions.q: In a segmentation system, segment 2 has base 4300 and limit 400. What is the physical address for the logical address (segment 2, offset 53)?
questions.exp: Offset 53 < limit 400, so physical address = base + offset = 4300 + 53 = 4353.

questions.q: Which allocation method avoids external fragmentation and also supports efficient direct access?
questions.exp: An index block lists the data blocks, so any block can be reached directly with no external fragmentation.

questions.q: A system has 4 processes, each needing at most 3 units of the same resource type. What is the minimum number of resource units that guarantees the system is deadlock-free?
Which statement about a multilevel feedback queue scheduler is correct?
options: It cannot use Round Robin in any queue
It requires prior knowledge of exact burst times
Processes can move between queues, which also helps prevent starvation
Processes are permanently assigned to one queue
questions.exp: MLFQ promotes and demotes processes among queues based on behaviour and waiting time, so aging can prevent starvation.

questions.q: The main goal of multiprogramming is to:
options: speed up a single program on many cores
maximize CPU utilization by keeping several jobs in memory so the CPU is never idle
questions.exp: When one job waits for I/O, the CPU switches to another job in memory.

questions.q: A system has 10 identical units of one resource. Allocations are P0 = 3, P1 = 2, P2 = 2 and maximum needs are P0 = 7, P1 = 4, P2 = 5. Which of the following is NOT a safe sequence?
questions.exp: Available = 10 - 7 = 3; needs: P0 4, P1 2, P2 3. P0 cannot go first (4 > 3), so any sequence starting with P0 is unsafe. P1 or P2 can start (e.g. P1, P2, P0 and P2, P0, P1 are safe).

questions.q: Preemptive SJF (SRTF) with P1 (arrival 0, burst 7), P2 (2, 4), P3 (4, 1), P4 (5, 4). What is the average waiting time?
Preemptive priority scheduling (smaller number = higher priority): P1 (arrival 0, burst 5, priority 2) and P2 (arrival 1, burst 3, priority 1). At what time does P1 complete?
questions.exp: P1 runs 0-1, preempted by P2 (1-4), then P1 resumes 4-8 for its remaining 4 ms.

questions.q: Consider FCFS scheduling for processes P1 (arrival 0, burst 5), P2 (arrival 1, burst 3), P3 (arrival 2, burst 8). What is the average waiting time?
questions.exp: P1 starts at 0 (WT 0), P2 starts at 5 (WT 4), P3 starts at 8 (WT 6); average = 10/3 = 3.33.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a method of recovering from deadlock?
options: Aborting processes one at a time until the cycle is broken
Increasing the time quantum of the CPU scheduler
questions.exp: Recovery uses process termination or resource preemption; changing the quantum has no effect on the deadlock.

questions.q: Which statement about a monitor is correct?
options: Several processes may execute monitor procedures simultaneously
At most one process can be active inside the monitor at any time
The programmer must explicitly code P and V for mutual exclusion
Condition variables are implemented using busy waiting
questions.exp: A monitor is a language construct that guarantees mutual exclusion automatically: only one process is active inside at a time. Condition variables (wait/signal) provide synchronisation within it.

questions.q: The starting address of the Interrupt Service Routine is obtained from the:
questions.exp: The interrupt number indexes the vector table, which holds ISR addresses.

questions.q: In the bounded-buffer producer-consumer solution with a buffer of N slots, the semaphores empty, full and mutex are initialised respectively to:
questions.exp: empty counts free slots (N), full counts filled slots (0) and mutex guards buffer access (1).

questions.q: A C program calls fork() three times in sequence (no conditions). How many child processes are created in total?
questions.exp: Total processes = 2³ = 8, including the original, so 7 are children.

questions.q: SJF scheduling predicts the next CPU burst by exponential averaging: τ(n+1) = α·t(n) + (1-α)·τ(n). If α = 0.5, the initial prediction τ0 = 10 ms and the first actual burst t0 = 6 ms, what is the next prediction τ1?
Thrashing occurs in a virtual memory system when:
options: the CPU is idle because no process is ready
a process spends more time paging than executing
questions.exp: Excessive page faults, often from too high a degree of multiprogramming, cause thrashing.

questions.q: In Unix, the three standard file descriptors 0, 1 and 2 correspond to:
questions.exp: By convention 0 is standard input, 1 standard output, 2 standard error.

questions.q: A process that has been swapped out of main memory to disk while waiting for an event is in the state called:
questions.exp: In the seven-state model the medium-term scheduler can swap a blocked process out; it then sits in the blocked-suspended state until the event occurs and then becomes ready-suspended.

questions.q: In the access-matrix model of protection, storing the matrix column-wise (for each object, the list of domains and their rights) gives:
questions.exp: Columns are objects, so storing a column per object yields an ACL (per-object list). Storing rows (per-domain list of objects and rights) yields capability lists.

questions.q: Spooling is mainly used to:
options: switch between user mode and kernel mode
overlap I/O of one job with computation of others, e.g. queuing print jobs on disk
questions.exp: Spooling uses disk as a large buffer so slow devices like printers can be shared efficiently.

questions.q: When a parent process terminates before its child, the child process is adopted by:
options: the shell that started the parent
questions.exp: Orphaned children are re-parented to init/systemd (PID 1), which reaps them on exit.

questions.q: What is 'cycle stealing' in DMA?
options: The CPU takes extra clock cycles from the DMA
The DMA controller takes the memory bus for a few cycles, delaying the CPU
Instruction cycles are skipped to save power
Two processes share one CPU cycle
questions.exp: In cycle-stealing mode, DMA transfers one word at a time by briefly taking over the bus.

questions.q: A 16 GB disk has 4 KB blocks. A bit-vector (bitmap) is used for free-space management with one bit per block. What is the size of the bitmap?
questions.exp: Blocks = 2^34 / 2^12 = 2^22 bits = 2^19 bytes = 512 KB.

questions.q: A process arrives at time 4, has a CPU burst of 6 ms and completes at time 20 (waiting only in the ready queue). What is its waiting time?
questions.exp: Turnaround = 20 - 4 = 16; waiting = turnaround - burst = 16 - 6 = 10.

questions.q: Which page replacement algorithm is free from Belady's anomaly?
questions.exp: LRU and Optimal are stack algorithms; the set of pages in n frames is always a subset of that in n+1 frames.

questions.q: What is the key difference between a mutex and a binary semaphore?
options: A mutex has ownership: only the thread that locked it should unlock it
A binary semaphore cannot be used for signalling
A mutex can take any non-negative integer value
A mutex is used only between processes
questions.exp: Mutexes are owned by the locking thread, whereas a binary semaphore can be signalled by a different thread.

questions.q: The command kill -9 1234 does what?
options: Sends the SIGKILL signal, forcibly terminating process 1234
questions.exp: Signal 9 is SIGKILL, which cannot be caught or ignored.

questions.q: Memory has free partitions of 100, 500, 200, 300 and 600 KB (in order). Processes of 212, 417, 112 and 426 KB arrive in that order. Which strategy can place all four processes?
questions.exp: Best fit: 212→300, 417→500, 112→200, 426→600. First fit and worst fit leave 426 KB unplaced.

questions.q: A counting semaphore is initialised to 10. Then 14 P (wait) operations and 9 V (signal) operations are completed on it. What is the final value of the semaphore?
questions.exp: Final value = 10 - 14 + 9 = 5.

questions.q: The time taken by the dispatcher to stop one process and start another running is called:
questions.exp: Dispatch latency is the time for the dispatcher to perform the context switch and resume a process.

questions.q: Two threads each execute the single statement count = count + 1 (not atomic) on a shared variable with initial value 5. Which set contains all possible final values?
questions.exp: If both read 5 before either writes, the result is 6 (lost update); otherwise 7. 5 is not possible.

questions.q: In the many-to-one multithreading model, which is a major drawback?
options: Thread creation requires a kernel call
Each user thread needs a kernel thread
If one thread makes a blocking system call, the entire process blocks
questions.exp: All user threads map to one kernel thread, so a blocking call blocks all of them and there is no parallelism on multiprocessors.

questions.q: A process that has finished execution but still has an entry in the process table because its parent has not yet called wait() is known as a:
questions.exp: A terminated child whose exit status has not been collected by the parent remains as a zombie.

questions.q: In a resource-allocation graph where every resource type has a single instance, a cycle indicates that:
options: the system is in a safe state
a deadlock may or may not exist
questions.exp: With single-instance resources, a cycle is both necessary and sufficient for deadlock.

questions.q: Semaphore x is initialised to 0. Process P1 executes: S1; signal(x). Process P2 executes: wait(x); S2. What is guaranteed?
options: S1 and S2 execute at the same time
questions.exp: P2 blocks on wait(x) until P1 signals after S1, enforcing the order S1 then S2.

questions.q: Which of the following instructions can be executed only in kernel (privileged) mode?
options: Loading a value from the user's own memory
Instructions that perform I/O or modify the memory-management registers
Jumping to another instruction in the program
questions.exp: Privileged instructions such as direct I/O and MMU changes are restricted to kernel mode to protect the system.
